## Intro

- Welcome to Finance 1!
- Classes: Mondays and Wednesdays, 15:30 - 17:30;
- Office hours: Fridays, 9:00 - 10:00, or by appointment;
- Class github repository: [https://github.com/epge-classes/finance-1-2026](https://github.com/epge-classes/finance-1-2026);
- This is the first class of a _sequence_;
- Finance 2 next quarter, from Felipe Iachan;
- If you ever want to be advised by me, you _have_ to take both classes;

## What I _think_ we will cover
This is a **foundational** course in Asset Pricing. Topics include:

- No-arbitrage and the stochastic discount factor;
- Linear factor models and beta-representation of asset returns;
- Consumption-based asset pricing and the Equity Premium Puzzle;
- Habit models, long-runs risk models, and rare disasters;
- A bit of option pricing and non-parametric recovery of the SDF;
- Interest rate models and their term structure;
- A bit of Machine Learning in Asset Pricing;

## Useful info

- Attendance is not mandatory, but highly recommended;
- Slides will be available before class on Github;
- The material will be scattered across books and papers -- I will cite everything;
- I will **not** teach on Jan 21st and on Jan 26th (away for a conference). Good dates for make-up classes?
- There are no exams, and no problem sets -- more on evaluation later;

## Evaluation

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}
**[Research Proposal (50%)](https://github.com/epge-classes/finance-1-2026/blob/main/Instructions_Research_Proposal.md)**

- Individual assignment;
- 5-10 pages;
- Research question + motivation + contribution + feasibility;
- Check-in: two-paragraph summary by end of week with lecture 10;
- You should start reading what's published in top journals _now_;
- Due date: TBD

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**[Paper Presentation (35%)](https://github.com/epge-classes/finance-1-2026/blob/main/Instructions_Paper_Presentation.md)**

- Present one paper related to your proposal;
- Graded on delivery (50%), slides (35%), Q&A (15%);
- Goal: make everyone understand why your proposal matters;
- Check-in: propose paper by end of week with lecture 10;

\vspace{0.6em}

**[Peer Review (15%)](https://github.com/epge-classes/finance-1-2026/blob/main/Instructions_Research_Proposal.md#peer-review)**

- Review one classmate's proposal, 2 pages maximum;
- Due one week after proposal deadline
:::
:::

## Useful books
**Books**: (in no particular order)
\footnotesize

- Cochrane, J. H. (2005). [*Asset Pricing*](https://www.johnhcochrane.com/asset-pricing) (Revised Edition). Princeton University Press.
- Campbell, J. Y. (2017). [*A Course in Asset Pricing*](https://press.princeton.edu/books/hardcover/9780691160801/financial-decisions-and-markets). Princeton University Press.
- Campbell, J. Y., Lo, A. W., & MacKinlay, A. C. (1997). [*The Econometrics of Financial Markets*](https://press.princeton.edu/books/hardcover/9780691043012/the-econometrics-of-financial-markets). Princeton University Press.
- Back, K. (2017). [*Asset Pricing and Portfolio Choice Theory*](https://www.amazon.com/Portfolio-Financial-Management-Association-Synthesis/dp/0190241144). Oxford University Press.
- Duffie, D. (2001). [*Dynamic Asset Pricing Theory*](https://www.amazon.com.br/Dynamic-Asset-Pricing-Theory-Third/dp/069109022X). Princeton University Press.
- Tuckman, B., & Serrat, A. (2022). [*Fixed Income Securities: Tools for Today's Markets*](https://www.amazon.com.br/Fixed-Income-Securities-Todays-Markets/dp/1119835550). Wiley.
- Singleton, K. J. (2006). [*Empirical Dynamic Asset Pricing: Model Specification and Econometric Assessment*](https://press.princeton.edu/books/hardcover/9780691122977/empirical-dynamic-asset-pricing). Princeton University Press.
- Veronesi, P. (2010). [*Fixed Income Securities*](https://www.wiley.com/en-us/Fixed+Income+Securities%3A+Valuation%2C+Risk%2C+and+Risk+Management%2C+1st+Edition-p-9780470586891). Wiley.
- Hull, J. C. (2021). [*Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives*](https://www.amazon.com/Options-Futures-Other-Derivatives-Global/dp/1292410655). Pearson.
